newsitem.title: USA: Olympics bomb suspect will get look at FBI files.
newsitem.headline: Olympics bomb suspect will get look at FBI files.

text.p: Former Olympics security guard Richard Jewell will be allowed to examine sealed FBI documents from search warrant affidavits that lay out the grounds for federal suspicion against him, a magistrate ruled on Friday.

According to a copy of the 11-page order obtained by Reuters, federal officials have one week to provide Jewell and his attorneys with witness information that could shed light on what led FBI investigators to his door.

Issued late Friday by U.S. Magistrate Gerrilyn Brill, the order raised the possibility that Jewell's attorneys would be able to determine whether the federal government had probable cause to secure four search warrants against their client and to name him as a suspect in the case.

Jewell, 33, a former police officer, has been the only suspect identified in the investigation into the July 27 bombing, which left two dead and more than 100 injured at Centennial Olympic Park in downtown Atlanta.

Initially hailed as a hero for discovering a green knapsack that contained the homemade pipe bomb, Jewell has steadfastly maintained his innocence while being hounded by the news media and tailed by FBI agents for nearly seven weeks.
Armed with search warrants issued between July 30 and Aug. 3, investigators conducted an extensive search of Jewell's suburban Atlanta apartment, his pickup truck and a rural cabin.
Kent Alexander, the U.S. Attorney in Atlanta who opposed an earlier attempt to unseal affidavit documents, said his office will not try to stop the material from being unsealed.
"We are satisified with the order and we have no plans to appeal," he said in a statement.

The magistrate's order did not clear the way for the material to be made public. It also restricted Jewell from reviewing documents detailing the makeup of the pipe bomb and disclosing FBI investigation methods.
Jewell's criminal lawyer Jack Martin, speaking after the ruling, said he did not expect his client ever to be indicted in the bombing.
"The witness information in the affidavit will be revealed to the defence. That is information only the defence will be able to see," Martin told NBC's Atlanta-affiliate, WXIA-TV, in an interview.
"We are under strict instructions not to reveal that information to anyone else," he added.
Earlier this week, CBS News reported that the FBI investigation was focusing on a new suspect and several possible accomplices with no connection to Jewell.
Other news organisations subsequently said federal investigators had several new suspects, including one with links to the citizens' militia movement.
FBI agents also examined an olive-green duffel bag from an Army and Navy surpus store as part of their ongoing investigation into the Olympic park bombing.

Federal agents picked up the bag at a store in suburban Atlanta on Thursday, telling the store's owner they wanted to photograph it. The duffel bag, which sells for less than $30, was described as standard-issue for soldiers in the U.S. military.
